references.text: The guest says he will return and Sarah shall have a son – this is why they ask about Sarah.
God promises Abraham a son through Sarah – the background for the guests asking about her.
Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah’s tent – the tent that was Sarah’s dwelling place.
Paul quotes the promise from this visit: 'At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.'
By faith Sarah received power to conceive, even though she was past childbearing age, because she considered Him faithful who had made the promise.
The Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and Sarah bore a son for Abraham – the fulfillment of the promise given at this visit.
Connects the confirmation of the promise in the tent with the actual fulfillment of the birth.
Sarah’s role in the tent is a key part of God’s plan to maintain a righteous family.
